descriptions.description: Habitat: — Clinopodium arundanum occurs in the understorey and at the edge of forests dominated by Abies pinsapo Boiss. (pinsapares) or more rarely by Pinus pinaster Aiton, on north-facing slopes, between (860 –) 1100 – 1430 m a. s. l., under a Mediterranean climate in supra-mesomediterraneam thermotypes, whith annual rainfall exceeding 1000 mm. The Abies pinsapo forest of Los Reales Peak and its surrounding area, represents the last surviving stand on ultramafic soil of this fir, endemic to the Serranía de Ronda. Within this area, C. arundanum occurs in two main habitats, always on ultramafic soils. One habitat corresponds to the deeply shaded understorey of the pinsapares, under a dense canopy, growing on humic well-developed soils (Fig. 5). In this habitat lichens and mosses dominate, and vascular plants are scarce. Co-occurring angiosperms include Cerastium gibraltaricum Boiss., Festuca grex ampla Hack. and Rubia occidens Capelo, M. Seq. & H. Schaef. The second habitat corresponds to scree slopes within ravines with intermittent streams that cross the forested area, where the tree canopy is sparse or absent. It is in this habitat where C. arundanum reaches the highest densities. Here, C. arundanum grows among rock boulders (Fig. 5), and co-occurring taxa include Galium mollugo L., Scrophularia scorodonia L., Pteridium aquilinum (L.) Kunh, and other heliophilous plants such as Ulex baeticus Boiss. subsp. baeticus and Cistus populifolius L., as well as saxicolous taxa, namely Chaenorrhinum grex villosum (L.) Lange, and even higrophilous taxa in wet slopes as Erica terminalis Salisb. and Molinia caerulea (L.) Moench, in addition to the species mentioned for the understorey habitat. Biotic interactions: — Bees, including Amegilla sp. (Fig. 6 A) and cf. Colletes, butterflies (Fig. 6 B) and bee flies (Bombyliidae) were observed as flower visitors.

Phenology: — Flowering begins at the end of June, with full bloom in mid-July, continuing throughout August – September. Fruiting begins in July, and dispersal occurs from August onwards. At the end of September, most plants have already dispersed their fruits, or they are in fruit, however, it is not rare to find some individuals with flowers in anthesis.

Preliminary conservation status: — Clinopodium arundanum is documented by 17 herbarium collections, made between 1838 and 2025, and 3 observations. Taken together, these records represent 10 occurrences, all made in Los Reales de Sierra Bermeja, a Natura 2000 site, protected also as ‘ Paraje Natural Los Reales de Sierra Bermeja’. The 10 existing occurrences represent a single subpopulation consisting of an estimated 3,083 individuals (2025 census data), including 2,820 in Pinsapar de Los Reales, 30 in Pinsapar de la Mujer, 2 in Pinsapar del Castellón, all associated to stands of Spanish fir (Abies pinsapo), along with 231 individuals in Barranco del Algarrobo, in a stand of maritime pine (Pinus pinaster). A single location can be considered with respect to the most serious plausible threat of forest fires, to which Spanish fir forests, the main habitat of C. arundanum, are not resilient. Forest fires, which are expected to become more recurrent in the projected climate change scenarios, promote the growth of pine forests, where C. arundanum is less abundant, and of heliophilous shrublands dominated by Ulex baeticus subsp. baeticus, and Cistus populifolius, where C. arundanum has never been found. Its extent of occurrence (EOO) is calculated as 0.7 km 2, but since it is less than the AOO it is changed to 8 km 2 to equal the AOO for conceptual consistency, falling within the limits for Critically Endangered status under criterion B 1). Its area of occupancy (AOO) is estimated at 8 km 2 (within the limits for Critically Endangered status under criterion B 2). Given the high impact of stochastic events in small and geographically restricted populations, ex situ conservation, namely seed banking and cultivation at El Castillejo Botanical Gardens (El Bosque, Cádiz) — property of the Andalusian government, which focus is the flora of Serranía de Ronda — should also be regarded as a priority. Considering the extremely narrow EOO and AOO, the existence of a single location, and the inferred (e. g., 2021 forest fire) and projected continuing decline in habitat extent and quality, C. arundanum is thus assigned a preliminary risk of extinction status of Critically Endangered [CR B 1 ab (iii) + 2 ab (iii)].

Description: — Suffruticose perennial herb, prostrate, up 50 cm tall, villose-glandulose, slighty aromatic, with woody rhizomes and stock. Stems woody, slender, (0.5 –) 1 (– 1.5) mm in diameter, stoloniferous, very branched; in the upper part herbaceous and very leafy; hairy, densely villose-glandulose, with eglandular hairs 2 – 2.5 mm long, and glandular hairs 1 – 1.5 mm long. Leaves ovate to suborbicular, 10 – 15 (– 23) × 9 – 14 mm, with a length / width ratio of 0.9 – 1 (– 1.5), rounded at base, acute at apex, shallowly and remotely crenate-serrate, petiolate, villose-glandulose; eglandular hairs 2 – 2.5 mm long, glandular hairs 1 – 1.5 mm long, with sessile, globose glands on the abaxial surface; veins curved towards the apex; petiole shorter than blade, villose. Inflorescence cymose, in the apex of the aerial stems, formed by 1 – 3 (– 4) spaced verticillasters; axis densely villose-glandulose with long glandular and eglandular hairs; bracts similar to the leaves or ovate-elliptic, generally shorter than the verticillaster, with hairs and glands identical to those of the leaves; verticillaster up to 3 cm wide, with 6 – 14 flowers, bracteoles linear, as long as the tube calyx, with glandular and eglandular hairs up to 1.5 mm long. Calyx 10 mm long, bilabiate, subsessile with peduncle up to 1 mm long in flower, hidden by the villose-glandulose indumentum, peduncle accrescent and less hairy in fruit, calyx-tube 6 – 7 mm long, tubular, slightly curved, with 13 nerves, villose-glandulose outside, with glandular and eglandular hairs 1 – 1.5 mm long, sessile globose glands, and with a line of hairs inside on the distal half (carpostegium); upper lip with 3 teeth, triangular-subulate, 3 – 4 mm long; lower lip with 2 narrower teeth, triangular-subulate 4 – 5 mm long, all teeth with indumentun as tube. Corolla bilabiate, exert, resupinate, 13 – 14 mm long, laxly hairy; tube white; lips very pale lilac to whitish with the margins showing a more intense tonality, upper lip 3 - lobed, lower lip 1 - lobed, emarginate. Stamens didynamous, little exert, not extending beyond the lower lip, anthers purple, pollen white. Style slightly 2 - branched at the apex, with unequal branches, little exert, generally not extending beyond the lower lip. Nutlets ovoid, 1.25 × 1 mm, brown, smooth with a whitish insertion surface.

Distribution: — Narrowly endemic to the western limit of the Sierra Bermeja mountains. This mountain massif is situated in the southwestern part of the Baetic System (Fig. 4 A), in the Málaga province. Within Sierra Bermeja, C. arundanum occurs exclusively on the northern slope of Los Reales Peak and its surrounding area (Fig. 4 B), which are protected under Andalusian law as Paraje Natural Los Reales de Sierra Bermeja.
Etymology: — Boissier´s species name ‘ arundana’, derives from Arunda, the ibero-roman old name for the town currently named Ronda, the most important urban centre in the Serranía de Ronda territory.
